Thanks Samir — got the files. Attaching Redwood's redacted SOC 2 and a matching subprocessor inventory (CSV) that highlights which of our subprocessors may touch customer data and under what conditions.

Notes on our subprocessor mapping (high level):
- Cloud: AWS (us-west-2) — primary hosting, may process encrypted customer content in transit and at rest. We use per-customer encryption keys where requested; KMS integration details in the attached CSV.
- Caching/kv: In-house optimized KV cache running on dedicated instances in the same VPC; no direct third-party caching vendor.
- Logging/Observability: Datadog (logs/metrics only). Logs are redacted and PII/PHI is never stored in logs per default configuration; we can enable additional redaction for enterprise customers.
- Analytics: Mixpanel for product telemetry (event-level, not content).
- Third-party classifiers: We use an opt-in content classifier from VerityAI for moderation during pre-processing; classifier runs in our VPC and does not store raw content.

Requested next steps from Redwood:
1) Dev (cc) will provide a simple data flow diagram focusing on the components that touch customer content and how keys are managed — ETA EOD 6/22.
2) We'll start the vendor questionnaire and return initial answers by 6/28, earlier if possible.

If procurement wants, we can schedule a 30-minute security sync on 6/24 or 6/25. What works best for your team?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
